docs.title: Augmented Software Engineering
docs.text:
Build software. Use AI. Understand what you build.

A practical foundation in software engineering, the tools professionals use every day, and the AI-assisted workflows that are changing how software gets made.

Start here View roadmap

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
This handbook is the learning environment for the Augmented Software Engineering program at Holberton School Albania.

It teaches software engineering the way it is practised now: with AI assistants in the editor, the terminal and the code review. You will use those assistants from the start. You will also learn enough of the fundamentals to check what they produce, fix it when it is wrong, and explain every line you ship.

docs.title: How you will work
docs.text:
• Build first

    Every topic ends in something that runs. You learn a concept by using it, breaking it and fixing it.

  • AI as a pair, not a replacement

    You will prompt, review and correct AI output. The assistant writes a draft; you are responsible for what gets merged.

  • Understand what you ship

    If you can't explain it, you don't commit it. Reading code and debugging matter as much as writing it.

  • Work like a professional

    Git, pull requests, code review and a real development environment from the first day.

docs.title: The journey
docs.text:
• 1 · Tools

    Set up your machine and learn the tools you will use every day: the terminal, WSL, VS Code, Git and GitHub.

    Explore Tools

  • 2 · Foundations

  • 5 · Projects

    Explore Projects

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Five stages, each building on the one before. You start with the tools, learn the fundamentals, build real software, bring AI into the workflow, and finish with projects that show what you can do.

Curriculum in progress

The program is being finalized. Stages and topics below show the intended path; details will change as each section is published. Stages marked in grey are not open yet.

docs.title: Learning path
docs.text:
1 Tools Set up

A working development environment and the tools used throughout the program.

Terminal WSL VS Code Git GitHub

By the end of this stage you can:

  • open a terminal and move around your machine with confidence
  • write, run and debug code in VS Code
  • track your work with Git and publish it on GitHub

Go to Tools

2 Foundations Learn the core

The core knowledge every software engineer relies on, whether or not an assistant is writing the first draft.

By the end of this stage you can:

  • write programs that use variables, control flow, functions and data structures
  • reason about how a program runs and why it fails
  • read unfamiliar code and explain what it does
3 Software Development Build

How software is designed, built, tested, debugged and maintained by a team.

By the end of this stage you can:

  • structure a project so that others can read and change it
  • write tests and use them to catch regressions
  • work through pull requests and code review
4 Augmented Engineering Augment

AI as part of the everyday engineering workflow, used with judgement.

By the end of this stage you can:

  • use AI assistants to plan, write, refactor and document code
  • review generated code for correctness, security and style
  • decide when to use an assistant and when not to
5 Projects Ship

Practical projects that bring the different skills together into a portfolio.

By the end of this stage you can:

  • take a project from idea to a deployed, documented result
  • show your work and explain the decisions behind it

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Before you write real software, you need a place to write it. This section sets up your machine and teaches the tools you will use every day of the program.

Stage 1 No prerequisites

Work through the tutorials in order. Each one assumes the one before it is done.

  • Zero Day

    What to expect, what to install first, and how the program works.

    Start

  • WSL

    Run Linux on Windows, the environment most of the program uses.

    Set up WSL

  • VS Code

    Your editor: extensions, the integrated terminal, and an AI assistant in the loop.

    Set up VS Code

  • Git & GitHub

    Track every change, collaborate without conflicts, and publish your work.

    Learn Git

On macOS or Linux?

You can skip the WSL tutorial. Everything else applies as written.
